response: No, the transverse apex does not always coincide with the coronal apex in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. The transverse apex refers to the point of maximum rotation in the transverse plane, while the coronal apex refers to the point of maximum curvature in the coronal plane. Studies have shown that the transverse and coronal apices can be different, with the transverse apex often being more proximal (closer to the spine) than the coronal apex. This discrepancy can have implications for surgical planning and correction of the deformity.
